label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S PROTEST.

label: text
text: THREAT OF RETALIATIONS.

label: text
text: Allegations About Help for Wu Peizfu

label: text
text:
As Foreign Minister of the Nationalist Government at Canton, Mr. Eugene Chen has addressed a long protest to His Majesty's Consul-General.
Exception is taken—arguments being advanced—to the landing of the British Naval party at the Steamboat Co.'s wharves on Saturday, and the clearing opt of the strike pickets thereon.
Threat of retaliations—through the instrument of strike and boycott (a nation-wide economic weapon of Nationalist opinion, as it is called)—is made in the communique.

label: text
text: Further, the British are accused of din ulterior motive in hindering the Canton Government from pushing on towards victory against Wu Pei-fu.

label: text
text:
Act of Aggression.
The official communication ends:—

label: text
text: “I have the honour to protest against the forcible landing yesterday of,” armed British naval forces on the jetties in the West Bund of Canton—within a stone’s throw of the scene of the murders on June 23, 1925. This action is not only a violation of the Laws of Nations but in the actual circumstances of the moment it is an act of material and moral aggression that is calculated to lead to another British massacre of the Chinese in this city. Guns of your warships are trained on the busiest section of Canton’s great roadway. There also are the quarters of the strike pickets and a centre of the activities of the people who have been incensed by the notorious bandit and pirate’s speech of the Governor of Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Cunton, Sept. 6.

label: text
text: “The Hongkong Governor's exercise in vituperation was left officially unanswered because a reply to it invited and might have exacerbated public feeling and rendered impossible any further search for a new solution of the strike and boycott movement in this territory. And it is within your personal knowledge that during the past week I have been seriously considering an alternative solution which might bring about a speedy settlement on terms acceptable to both sides.

label: text
text:
Too Proud to Reply.
“The latter’s outburst, it is well known, instantly aroused the intensest indignation here, because it was at once a misrepresentation of the objective facts of the situation and a signal affront to a Government whose accredited representatives were still members (together with official representatives of the Government of Hong Kong) of a Conference formally under adjournment and not at an end.

label: paragraph_title
text: Some of the Arguments.

label: text
text: "It is in these circumstances that the British Naval authorities have thought fit to intervene. Neither in law nor on facts have they any right to do so. The jetties in question, besides being on Chinese territory, are Chinese public property which have only been leased to the Hongkong, Canton and Macao Steamboat Co. They have not been used by the Company for more than a year. They are constructed of iron and concrete and are admittedly in no danger of destruction. Nor is the Company under any risk of losing its property or leasing rights in them. No British lives are or have been in jeopardy or peril in connection with them. And proper Chinese authorities have never been notified or asked to afford protection to same."

label: text
text: "These are the facts of the case. But independently of these facts I have to remind you that there is no principle or rule of International Law nor is there any provision in any of the Treaties between China and Great Britain, or any other Treaty Powers, which can possibly justify or excuse the flagrant invasion of Chinese territorial sovereignty committed by the British Naval forces."

text: KING EDWARD RUMOURS

label: text
text: Rumours were current in town this morning about the possibility of a new hotel being established.

label: text
text: Formerly occupied by Messrs. Lune, Crawford, Ltd., are some premises in the upper floors of their old building, above the King Edward Hotel.

label: text
text: (One-rumour was that the King Edward Hotel were taking over these extra floors and thus increasing their accommodation.

label: text
text: On reference to Mr. J. Mitchell, the popular manager, the “China Mail” was informed that the King Edward was not taking over these upper floors at present.

label: text
text: Another rumour was that a nev concern, to be called the Savo Hotel had the matter under consideration.

label: text
text: Messrs. Leong Hing Kee of the Metropole Hotel and the Hong-kong fish Store are said to be interested in this project.

label: paragraph_title

No confirmation of this report was available on enquiries being made this morning.

label: text
text: Canton were some British colonial port under coercion, but British Naval forces have gone about their job in a manner fitly designed to goad an indignant and inflamed public to retaliatory action and to create an incident that would infallibly disable the Nationalist Government from effectively prosecuting its present victorious campaign in central China against Wu Pei-fu, who is widely reported to be supported by the British.

label: text
text: “The creation of such an incident being, it is believed, the political objective of the British Naval operation the Nationalist Government is determined not to be drawn into it. Once recently at Wuchow the Nationalist Government had to protest against an attempt to create a similar incident planned (it is significant to note) by the same British Naval forces. It may be—it is—a grievous humiliation that Nationalist China is unable to repel by force of arms such British Naval acts of war.

label: text
text:
But there is a powerful section of Chinese Nationalist opinion that believes in the application in a nation-wide scale of the economic weapon of the strike-and-boycott statesman in Britain's dealings with this country. But if it is true that England's foreign trade is her very lifeblood, it is clear that a real and national adoption of this view is immaterial to British policy in China then the rough-neck method of the sailor can continue to replace the mind and technique of the (?) in retaliation for the humiliations and insulting blows which England's "gunboat policy" is heaping on Nationalist China.
What British Policy Should Be!

label: text
text: A claim for stevedorage aboard the s.s. "President Cleveland" formed the subject of a claim at the Summary Court this morning. The Ming Kee Company sued Mr. Finn Malm, marine surveyor, coal merchant and ship's broker, for $200.

label: text
text: Mr. J. O'Donoghue appeared for plaintiffs and stated that the work in question was done on September 3 of last year. The agreement was that the work of loading and unloading should be done at the rate of 19 cents per ton.

label: text
text: Owing to circumstances with which he was not altogether familiar, said Mr. O'Donoghue, although he believed it had something to do with the action of the Dollar Line, the work was never completed. 900 tons had been handled out of 1,800 and this, at the agreed rate, would have work

text: AGITATORS BUSY.

label: paragraph_title

DEMONSTRATIONS IN.
SHANGHAI.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai; Sept. 7.

label: text
text: The students and labour agitators are planning large demonstrations today—the 25th anniversary of the signing of the Boxer Protocol.

label: text
text: The authorities have taken all precautions.

label: text
text: The Volunteers and the Police Reserves have been partially ordered to mobilise this morning.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Only Four Arrests.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, Sept. 7.

label: text
text: This morning the labour agitators and students held a mass meeting at the west gate of the native city, after which. large crowds proceeded to. Nanking Road, creating a din and throwing pamphlets in the air.

label: text
text: " The Police, aided by special constables, dispersed all gatherings till noon, and succeeded in preserving order, only four arrests being made.

label: text
text: No acts of violence have so far been reported.

label: text
text: Half of the Volunteer Corps are standing by, but so far they have not been called out.—Reuter.

text: Defendant continued that as a reward for his long service he was instrumental in getting them the work and if they had done it properly it would have been a fine business bringing in $8,000 or $10,000 a year. The work was not done properly and the plaintiff had not got on board himself to supervise as he had promised.

text: As this amounted to $162.45, Mr. Justice Wood said that he did not think anything that happened afterwards needed to be taken into consideration and he indicated that he would give judgment for this amount.

label: paragraph_title
text: DRIVER'S ALL NIGHT RIDE.

label: text
text: TO-DAY'S CASES.

label: text
text: The usual weekly list of traffic prosecutions came for hearing before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning. Dr. H. Speth, of the Netherlands Harbour Works, North Point, charged his Chinese driver with taking his motor car out without permission.

label: text
text: The incident of an all night outing with the car during Dr. Speth's absence at Macao was reported to him on his arrival, and this was verified by looking into the gasoline consumption.

label: text
text: The driver, who is no longer in the employment of the complaint, was fined $5.

label: text
text: A taxicab driver's offence was that of driving his vehicle in a reckless manner regardless of consequences.

label: text
text: Sub-Inspector Alexander, who was on a motor cycle patrol round on the day of the "offence", stated in evidence that he saw the taxi taking the bend at the foot of Lower Albert Road at a speed which he thought was about 25 miles an hour. The vehicle kept going on the wrong side of the road and swerved round another car. He pointed out that the danger was increased by the wet conditions at the time.

label: paragraph_title
text: "TALAMBA" ARRIVES.

label: paragraph_title
text: The Origin of the Trouble.

label: text
text: DUE TO MURDER.

label: text
text: Rice-Pots Thrown On Attempted. Intervention

label: paragraph_title
text: Intervention.

label: text
text: The A.S. "Talamba," which experienced trouble with mutinous deportress between Singapore and Hong Kong arrived in Kowloon Bay late last night and remained there during this morning. Police launches took over from the "Carlisle" party the duty of affording protection in the event of trouble, remaining there throughout the night.

label: text
text: This morning launches were engaged in removing the 64 de- portees from the ship and as soon as this was completed, the "Talamba" went alongside the wharf at Kowloon, arriving there shortly after one o'clock.

label: paragraph_title
text: European Passengers.

label: text
text: Including the deportees, there were 1,100 deck passengers on board and eleven Europeans in cabins. It appears from further particulars to hand since the arrival of the vessel that the origin of the trouble was entirely between the deportees themselves. A dispute arose as a result of which one man was killed by another. A general melee followed in the course of which two others were stabbed. The friends of the murdered man attempted to seize the alleged murderer but ten of the Sikh guards (from the Singapore police) who had been placed in charge of the deportees, (prevented them

label: paragraph_title
text: A Hasty Retreat

label: text
text: Objecting to interference in what they considered was the meeting out of justice the row assumed a graver aspect and became an insubordination. Attempts were made to break from the quarters below the hatchway where they were under guard. A party of officers who went below were received by a shower of rice bowls thrown at them by the mutinous deportees.

label: text
text: It may be mentioned in connection with the transportation of deportees by sea that it is not permissible to handcuff them because of possibilities of shipwreck.

label: text
text: Attempts were made to rush the doorway and the officers decided in view of the "dangerous temper shown and the number" of deportees, to withdraw the guards and barricade the door.

label: paragraph_title
text: “Macedonia” Assists.

label: text
text: This was done, the door locked, and large blocks of wood piled against it. Attempts to break down the barricade failed but the hours which followed were anxious ones for the handful of officers aboard. Wireless messages were sent but failed to reach Hongkong direct. The P. and O. liner, "Macedonia," however, on the way from Hong Kong to Singapore, picked up the messages and passed them on to the Hongkong Naval authorities.

label: text
text: These were received here on Sunday night (the trouble on the "Talamba" commenced on Sunday morning when the vessel was within 600 miles of Hongkong). H.M.S. "Carlisle," which had only arrived in Swatow a few hours before, was ordered to the assistance of the officers but owing to trouble experienced at Swatow bar she was unable to arrive on the scene until shortly after noon yesterday.

label: paragraph_title
text: All-night Vigil.
